topics.title: Is It a Compound Sentence?
topics.hint: A compound sentence has two complete short sentences joined by a comma and a joining word: , and  / , but  / , or  (also , so).
topics.source: grammar printable 1.4.4 + practice sheet + revision sheet

items.text: Check the weather before a hike, or you might get rained on.
My job is to feed the pets and give them water.
items.explanation: Only one subject and one verb idea: 'feed' and 'give' share the same subject.

items.text: Aiden picked apples, and we made a pie with them.
Would you like a salad, a sandwich, or soup for lunch?
items.explanation: 'or' joins things in a list, not two complete sentences.

items.text: The rain is making puddles. The street is wet.
items.explanation: These are two separate sentences. A compound sentence joins them with , and / , but / , or.

items.text: We went to the shelter, and we adopted a dog.
The strawberries are sweet, but the grapes are sour.
I have a lot of paper, I need more pencils.
items.explanation: There is a comma but no joining word (and / but / or).

items.text: Hand me the book, or put it on the table.
The play was good, but it lasted too long.
We can go to the park, or we can stay home.
The sun is bright. The sky is clear.
I brought a snack, and I shared it with my friend.
You can take the red pencil or the blue one.
The teacher smiled, but the class was noisy.
My brother likes apples. My sister likes oranges.
We packed our bags, and we left early for the trip.
It's raining outside, but I forgot my umbrella.
I wanted to go outside, but it was too cold.
Tom finished his homework.
She goes to the park on Sundays.
Rita was tired, so she went to bed early.
I watched a scary movie.
I wanted to travel, but I didn't have enough money.

topics.title: Pick the Joining Word
topics.instruction: Choose the joining word that completes the compound sentence.
topics.hint: Use AND to add. Use BUT when the two ideas are different. Use OR when there is a choice. Don't forget the comma before it!

topics.title: Combine with a Compound Predicate
topics.instruction: Choose the sentence that has one subject and two actions.
topics.hint: Say the subject only once, then join the two actions with AND or OR. No second subject and no comma.

items.text: Jani cleaned. Jani listened to music.
options: Jani cleaned and listened to music.

topics.title: Compound Subject or Compound Predicate?
topics.instruction: Does the sentence have a compound subject (C.S) or a compound predicate (C.P)?
topics.hint: Compound SUBJECT: two or more people or things do ONE action (Tom AND Sam ran). Compound PREDICATE: ONE doer does two or more actions (Tom ran AND jumped).
